messages:
alex (eng-runtime): noticing a spike in p95/p99 for text-generation today, started ~09:02 UTC, customers reporting slower responses and some 500s

mia (eng-sre): saw alerts from latency watcher too. p95 jumped from 180ms to 850ms on gpu-pool-3 between 09:00-09:10

raj (oncall): any OOMs in logs? p95 often comes from OOM-heavy fallback thrashing

alex (eng-runtime): checking logs now. here's the snippet from runtime logs right when the spike started:
```
2026-04-21T09:01:58Z WARN serving: request queued longer than target 120ms
2026-04-21T09:02:05Z ERROR gpu0: Alloc failed for 512MB, available 1.2GB, fragmentation high
2026-04-21T09:02:05Z ERROR model: OOM during KV-append, evict failed
2026-04-21T09:02:07Z INFO fallback-router: rerouting to smaller-quant model (gpt-6b-q4) for 12 requests
```

sara (support): customers complaining that chat sessions that run long get slow — sounds like KV cache growth and fragmentation? one user gave us a repro: 60 messages, avg 800 tokens each in a single convo

mia (eng-sre): that matches: KV growth + allocator fragmentation. GPU memory isn't a single contiguous chunk, small free slots scattered. when we try to allocate a large contiguous block for attention we get failure and then fallback, which increases latency

alex (eng-runtime): repro steps I'm running locally to confirm:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"rwd/gpt-6b","messages": [lots of exchanges] }'
2) tool to stream and keep session alive so KV cache builds
3) check runtime /metrics and `kubectl logs` for OOM lines

raj (oncall): quickly checked gpu node via ssh, running `nvidia-smi` shows allocated memory high and several small free chunks reported by our allocator plugin. ps output indicates many long-lived worker processes

alex (eng-runtime): pasted allocator diagnostic from node (shortened):
```
Allocator: cuda-mempool-v2
Total GPU: 24GiB
Used: 21.4GiB
Free fragments: 312 (avg 76KiB)
Largest free chunk: 128MiB
High-watermark: 22.0GiB
KV-cache accounted: 5.8GiB (sessions: 142 active)
```

mia (eng-sre): hmm largest free chunk 128MiB insufficient for some attention allocations that need ~512MiB contiguous -> triggers fallback and extra copies -> latency spike

alex (eng-runtime): initial mitigations I pushed:
- reduced per-request `max_new_tokens` default from 2048 -> 1024 for affected model group
- TTL on session KV cache lowered from 24h -> 1h (hotfix flag)
Both rolled as feature flags to prod in the last 10m

sara (support): have we messaged customers about temporary perf impact? ops-bot posted incident but needs short blurb

ops-bot: incident-12345 created: "p95 regressions due to GPU fragmentation / KV growth". Priority: P2. Status: investigating.

raj (oncall): other mitigation: drain large-session pods off gpu-pool-3 and restart to free fragmented memory. I can cordon/drain a node when we're ready. this will cause brief capacity drop but avoids repeated fallback thrash

alex (eng-runtime): agree. plan: 1) continue flag reductions (max_tokens / kv-ttl) 2) sequentially cordon+restart two worst nodes (gpu-pool-3-node-4, node-7) 3) enable allocator compaction flag on runtime (experimental) 4) schedule followup to tune session eviction logic

mia (eng-sre): add to that: enable per-req cap on KV cache bytes via runtime flag `--kv-cache-max-bytes=200000000` for this pool so single sessions can't monopolize memory

alex (eng-runtime): yes, I pushed the runtime flag to the pool config: `kv_cache.max_bytes=200000000` and `kv_cache.default_ttl_secs=3600`. also toggled `allocator.compact_on_oom=true` (will log compaction events)

raj (oncall): draining node-4 now (kubectl cordon node-4 && drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data). will watch request latencies and fallback counts. ETA ~6 mins to reschedule heavy pods

(6 minutes pass)

raj (oncall): node-4 drain finished, pods rescheduled. immediate drop in fallback events and p95 improved from 850ms -> 320ms. p99 still elevated around 1.2s for a small subset

alex (eng-runtime): allocator compaction log after node restart:
```
2026-04-21T09:12:34Z INFO allocator: compaction started on gpu0
2026-04-21T09:12:34Z INFO allocator: moved 2.8GiB across blocks; reclaimed 1.9GiB contiguous
2026-04-21T09:12:35Z INFO allocator: compaction complete, largest free chunk: 1.7GiB
```

mia (eng-sre): good sign. continuing node-7 drain in 2m. also we'll keep metric alerts relaxed for p99 for the next 15m while things rebalance

sara (support): I'll update the customer facing note: say "We experienced a transient performance regression due to GPU memory fragmentation from long-running sessions. We've implemented temporary limits and restarted affected nodes; latency is improving. We're working on permanent fixes."

alex (eng-runtime): follow-ups to permanently address this:
- tune allocator defaults (auto-compaction thresholds, merge size)
- implement smarter KV eviction (LRU + size-aware eviction) and per-org quotas
- add background defrag task when GPU utilization < 40%
- tests to reproduce long KV growth in CI (synthetic long chat harness)

mia (eng-sre): owners? Alex + Raj for immediate infra/runtime changes. Research ticket for KV eviction and allocator improvements assigned to eng-runtime / eng-ml. Sara will keep comms. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and then close the incident if stable

alex (eng-runtime): assigning tickets: INFRA-712 (node drain/compaction ops) -> raj, RUNTIME-434 (kv limits + compaction flags) -> alex, EVAL-210 (long-chat CI harness) -> eng-ml

raj (oncall): node-7 drain complete. p95 median now ~210ms, p99 down to ~560ms. closing active incident window. will leave compaction logs on for 24h.

mia (eng-sre): thanks team. postmortem will include root cause (KV growth + allocator fragmentation), mitigation steps we did, and long-term action items. I'll draft it this afternoon.

sara (support): closing loop with affected customers now.

alex (eng-runtime): TL;DR: OOM-like allocation failures from fragmentation due to large KV caches for long sessions. Hotfixes: lower per-request tokens & KV TTL, cap per-session KV bytes, drain/restart fragmented nodes, enable allocator compaction. Long-term: smarter eviction, defrag background, allocator tuning.

mia (eng-sre): dropping follow-up notes into incident-12345. anyone else? otherwise I'll mark thread resolved after postmortem draft."
